---
title: "Git"
---

## Staging

**git status**

Get a summary of staged changes. Various formatting options exist.

**git add** *file*

Tracks *file* if it is untracked, and stages all changes made to it so far

**git rm** [--cached] *file*

Stages the deletion of *file* and deletes the file from your computer unless --cached is given

**git mv** *file* *newname*

Stages the renaming of *file* to *newname* and renames the file on your computer

**git diff** [--staged]

Shows changes made to files that haven't been staged yet. With --staged, instead shows changes that were staged but not committed yet

## Committing

**git commit** -m *msg* [-a]

Creates a commit with message *msg*. If -a is specified, stages all tracked files

**git commit** --amend

Replaces the last commit with a new commit including all newly staged changes

**git log** [-p] [-*n*]

Shows the commit log. If -p is specified, shows the commit diffs. If -*n* is specified, shows the last *n* commits. Various other options exist for formatting output and filtering the log based on time, author, modified file, specific strings, etc.

## Branching

**git branch**

Display all branches of the repository

**git branch** *newbranch*

Creates a local branch named *newbranch*

**git push** *remote* *branch*

Pushes the local branch *branch* to remote *remote*

**git branch** -d *oldbranch*

Deletes the branch *oldbranch*

**git push** *remote* --delete *branch*

Deletes the remote branch *remote*/*branch*

**git checkout** *branch*

Switches to branch *branch* and updates HEAD to point to that branch. Changes local files to *branch*'s progress

**git checkout** --track *remote*/*remotebranch*

Creates a local tracking branch which tracks the remote branch *remote*/*remotebranch*

**git merge** *branch2*

Merges branch2 into your current branch. If the merge can be done automatically, it will create a merge commit. Otherwise, files will be left in an unmerged state. **git status** will display these files. Fix the conflicts manually.

**Renaming a Branch**

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not rename branches that other collaborators are working on. If you rename the master/main branch, expect to break integrations, services, or build/release scripts.
:::

Run the following commands:

- git branch move *oldname* *newname*: Rename the branch locally
- git push --set-upstream *remote* *newname*: Push the name change to the remote
- git push *remote* --delete *oldname*: Delete the old branch from the remote origin

## Getting a Repository

**git init**

Turns the current working directory into a git repository

**git clone** *url* [*newname*]

Clones a git repository from the given url. If *newname* is specified, renames the repository folder to that.

## Remotes

**git remote** -v

Lists all remote repositories with URLs

**git remote** add *name* *url*

Adds a new remote with name *name* at url *url*. Also, **git remote** rename and **git remote** remove

**git push** *remote* *branch*

Pushes un-pushed commits to branch *branch* of remote *remote*

**git fetch** *remote* *branch*

Downloads data from remote *remote* and branch *branch* that you don't have, without merging it to your local work

**git pull** *remote* [*branch*]

Fetches data from remote *remote* and branch *branch* (if not specified, tries to use the upstream branch), then merges it with your work

## Help

Run **git help** *verb*, or **git** *verb* -h

## Configuration

**git config** [--global] *key* *value*

Sets config option *key* to *value*. By default sets the option only for the current repository, if --global specified sets it for the user.

**git config** [--show-origin] *key*

Shows the configuration value for option *key*. If --show-origin specified, shows which file (repo, user, or system) had the final say in the option

**git config** --list [--show-origin]

Lists all configuration options and values. If --show-origin specified, shows which file (repo, user, or system) had the final say in the option

## Tagging

**git tag**

Lists all tags in the repository

**git tag** -a *tag* -m *msg* [*checksum*]

Marks the current commit (or the commit specified by *checksum* if it's supplied) with tag *tag* and message *msg*

**git tag** -d *tag*

Deletes the tag *tag* on your local repository

**git push** *remote* --delete *tag*

Deletes the tag *tag* on a remote repository *remote*
